clue.text: Confused account in newspaper about British Library exhibition's opening

indicators.note: about is read as turned about, so the word for a newspaper runs backwards
an opening is the start, so only the first letter of exhibition is kept

blocks.note: rag is a slang word for a low-quality newspaper
B is the standard abbreviation for British
L is a common abbreviation for library
the first letter of exhibition

explanation.surface: A muddled report in a newspaper about the opening of a British Library show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' joins the definition to the wordplay: GAR (rag turned about) followed by B, L and E gives GARBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a garble is a jumbled or distorted version of a message or story.

clue.text: After game, university student remains for stew

blocks.note: Go is an ancient Asian board game
U is the usual abbreviation for university
L for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A student eats leftover stew after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' looks like a verb about the student staying on, but it is a noun: what is left after burning. L for a student comes from the British learner driver's plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Goulash is a Hungarian dish of meat and paprika cooked slowly, a kind of stew.

clue.text: Discovered in the Alhambra: Zorro's blade

indicators.note: something discovered inside a phrase is sitting there among its letters, waiting to be found

blocks.note: the run starts at the end of Alhambra and continues into Zorro

explanation.surface: Zorro's sword is found in the Alhambra palace in Granada.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon and the apostrophe are ignored; the letters run straight across the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A razor is a sharp cutting edge used for shaving, so it counts as a blade.

clue.text: Good books are put up online verbatim

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means writing it from bottom to top, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: lit, short for literature, is good writing in book form
taken as written, then turned upwards
read as 'on line': L is the abbreviation for line, placed on (after) the rest

explanation.surface: Great books are uploaded to the internet word for word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Online' looks like a single word about the internet, but split it as 'on line' and it supplies L at the foot of the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal and verbatim both describe something reproduced exactly, word for word, without alteration.

clue.text: Gosh — close to Biden securing victory!

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it tight, so the president's name wraps around the victory letter

blocks.note: by means near or close to
Joe is the first name of US president Biden
V for victory, as in the V sign

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at someone close to Biden winning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' looks like a hint to take Biden's last letter, but here it is simply BY, meaning near.
explanation.definitionFit: By Jove is an old-fashioned exclamation of surprise, just as gosh is a mild expression of astonishment.

clue.text: Country divided by stupid leader's sycophants

indicators.note: a country split in two by a letter has that letter sitting in the middle of it
the leader of a word is its first letter, so only the start of stupid is used

blocks.note: Yemen is a country on the Arabian peninsula
the first letter of stupid

explanation.surface: A nation split apart by the flatterers around a foolish ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stupid leader' suggests a foolish head of state, but leader just means the first letter of stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men always agree with their boss to please them, which is what sycophants do.

clue.text: Hate token punishment for accepting bribes

indicators.note: punishment suggests the words being knocked about and beaten into a different shape

blocks.note: all nine letters are used as the raw material

explanation.surface: A hated token penalty handed out to someone caught taking backhanders.
explanation.definitionFit: An official who is on the take is corrupt and regularly pockets illicit payments in return for favours.

clue.text: Serious from outset, deserve to be ahead

indicators.note: being ahead means coming first, so the word for deserve goes in front of the other piece

blocks.note: to earn something is to merit or deserve it
est. is the abbreviation for established, as in 'Est. 1850', marking when a business began

explanation.surface: Someone serious from the start, who has earned a place at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: EST, short for established, is the label on shop signs giving the year a business was founded, so it means from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest describes a person who is sincere, intense and not joking, which is the meaning of serious here.

clue.text: Concentrated on current within-home care

indicators.note: within places the symbol for current inside the word for home

blocks.note: pad is slang for a home or flat
I is the physics symbol for electric current
care and attention both mean looking after something closely

explanation.surface: Home care staff focused on the current situation.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'within-home care' makes it look like a type of nursing; ignore it and read within as a placement instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To concentrate is to focus the mind, and to have paid attention is to have done exactly that.

clue.text: Pointless, maybe, when heartily fazed after Question 1

indicators.note: heartily points to the heart of the word, so only its central letter is taken

blocks.note: QU is a standard abbreviation for question
the Roman numeral for one
the middle letter of the five in fazed

explanation.surface: A contestant flustered after the first question on a TV game show.
explanation.walkthrough: Pointless is a BBC television quiz show; 'maybe' signals that it is just one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointless is an example of a TV quiz, a game show where contestants answer general knowledge questions.

clue.text: Reorganisation of trains by Conservative is short-lived

indicators.note: a reorganisation moves things into new places, so the letters of trains are put in a fresh order

blocks.note: the six letters of trains, rearranged
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Conservative government's shake-up of the railways doesn't last long.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transitory lasts only a brief time before passing away, which is what short-lived means.

clue.text: Lighter and warmer finally, after a fire is lit

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word warmer, so its last letter is the one used
lit is slang for drunk, and drunken letters stagger out of their proper order

blocks.note: the five letters of a fire, rearranged
the last letter of warmer

explanation.surface: The room gets brighter and warmer once a fire is lit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lit' seems to describe the fire burning, but it is slang for drunk and signals the shuffle; 'after' puts R behind the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairer can mean paler in complexion or colouring, as with fair hair or skin, so lighter in shade.

clue.text: Indeed, writer taking drug became more profound

blocks.note: split as 'in deed': deed is the outer word and in says the rest goes inside it
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An author who took drugs did indeed grow more profound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indeed' looks like an emphatic opener, but split as 'in deed' it is both the container signal and the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: To deepen is to grow deeper, and something deeper in thought or feeling is more profound.

clue.text: Sweet child's getting cold feeding ducks after bedtime

indicators.note: feeding something to ducks puts it into them, so one letter goes inside the others

blocks.note: CH is a standard abbreviation for child
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so two ducks are two zeros
C for cold, as on a tap
after bedtime is late

explanation.surface: A child gets chilly feeding the ducks when they should already be in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a batter's score of zero, so ducks gives the two O letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate is a confection, and in British usage a sweet is any individual item of confectionery.

clue.text: Applaud workers supporting strike

indicators.note: in a down clue, a supporting piece holds up the other from below, so it comes second

blocks.note: to clap is to strike, as in clap someone on the back
hands are manual workers, as in farmhands

explanation.surface: Cheering on the labourers who back an industrial strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests a walkout, but it is a blow; the workers sit underneath it in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To clap your hands is the physical act of applauding, showing approval by striking palms together.

clue.text: Hang around with barista, regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of barista is taken

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
the second, fourth and sixth letters of barista

explanation.surface: Loitering in the coffee shop with the person making the drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To wait is to stay in one place until something happens, which is what hanging around means.

clue.text: Beg to swap sides for fun

indicators.note: swapping sides means trading right for left, so one letter standing for a side is replaced by the other

blocks.note: to pray someone to do something is to beg them

explanation.surface: Pleading to change teams just for the enjoyment of it.
explanation.walkthrough: R for right becomes L for left in PRAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Play is activity done for enjoyment and amusement, so as a noun it can stand for fun.

clue.text: Army man's retiring

blocks.note: first meaning: a soldier of the lowest rank
second meaning: shy and keeping to oneself

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a soldier leaving the service, but 'retiring' means reserved, not stopping work.
explanation.definitionFit: A private is the lowest rank of soldier, and a private person is reserved, withdrawn and shy.

clue.text: Puzzled when record on agent is recalled by old journalist

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the record-on-agent combination is written backwards

blocks.note: an LP is a long-playing vinyl record
a rep, or representative, acts as an agent
ex means former
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: Baffled when a veteran reporter remembers a disc made by an agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' sounds like memory, but here it sends LP-on-REP backwards; 'by old journalist' then adds EX and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Perplexed and puzzled both describe being confused and unable to understand something.

clue.text: In south London area with morning off, one's getting quite hungry

indicators.note: taking the morning off removes the two-letter abbreviation for morning from the area's name
in tells us to place the final piece inside the shortened place name

blocks.note: Peckham is a district of south London
a.m. is the abbreviation for morning
I for one, plus 's read as is

explanation.surface: Someone in Peckham who skipped breakfast is starting to feel hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: Peckham is a district of south London. 'One's' is read as one is, I for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Peckish is an informal British word for being slightly hungry, wanting a snack.

clue.text: Drawing level at close of day?

blocks.note: first meaning: making the scores equal, as a verb form
second meaning: the time when daylight ends

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a match tied at dusk; the question mark flags that the two senses share one spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening up a score means equalising, while the evening is the period at the end of the day.

clue.text: Greek character's climbing entire central Doric column

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means going upwards, so the word is written bottom to top
central asks for the middle of the word Doric and nothing else

blocks.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
entire means all of it
the middle letter of the five in Doric

explanation.surface: A Greek climbing an entire Doric column in a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person, but it is a letter; Doric is a style of Greek column, which disguises the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar is an upright supporting post in a building, which is exactly what a column is.

clue.text: Things one wants whilst one's sick

indicators.note: something sick is out of sorts, so these letters are put out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written into the mix
I for one, plus 's read as is

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in bed drawing up a list of things they want.
explanation.definitionFit: A wish list itemises the things you would like to have, often presents or improvements.

clue.text: Dog expressed relief, picked up when it's time to be home

indicators.note: picked up as in heard by a listener, so we want a word that is spoken like the exclamation

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
phew is the sigh you let out when relieved

explanation.surface: A dog sighed with relief when it was time to go back indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A curfew is a rule setting the hour by which people must be indoors, so it is a set hour for getting back.

clue.text: Stick on horse to finish first in old Wild West show

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its end, so only the final letter of horse is kept
first in points to the opening letter of the word old

blocks.note: a rod is a stick
the last letter of horse
the first letter of old

explanation.surface: A rider stays on a bucking horse to win at a cowboy show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick on horse' paints a rider clinging on; in fact ROD comes first, then E and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a public exhibition of cowboy skills such as bronco riding, rooted in the American frontier.

clue.text: Staff, embracing new lines, love return of popular pasta dish

indicators.note: embracing means holding in its arms, so the staff word wraps round the letter for new
a return goes back the way it came, so the word for popular is read backwards

blocks.note: a cane is a walking staff
N is the abbreviation for new
L for line, doubled for the plural
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
something in is fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Restaurant staff, learning new lines, love the comeback of a favourite pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees but means a walking stick; the embracing only takes in the new letter, and the rest follow on behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannelloni are large pasta tubes stuffed and baked in sauce, served as an Italian main course.

clue.text: Daughter takes rent for weed

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
a rent is a tear or rip in cloth

explanation.surface: A daughter uses the money for her rent to buy cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' suggests payment and 'weed' suggests cannabis or a garden plant; both are misdirection, as a weed here is a feeble person.
explanation.definitionFit: A drip is British slang for a dull, feeble, spineless person, which is the informal sense of weed too.

clue.text: Make certain to head off criticism

indicators.note: with its head taken off, the word for criticism loses its first letter

blocks.note: censure is strong official criticism

explanation.surface: Taking steps to forestall complaints before they arise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like a verb meaning to forestall, but it tells you to remove the head letter of CENSURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure something is to guarantee that it happens, so the verb means making sure of it.

clue.text: Lots of people run in underpants

indicators.note: in places the letter for run inside the word for the underwear

blocks.note: a thong is a skimpy pair of underpants
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A crowd of people jogging in their underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a thong can also be a flip-flop, but here it is the underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A throng is a large crowd gathered together, so a great many individuals in one place.
